recognize_zh: 骨小樑表面的淺凹陷（Howship lacuna）中貼著一顆多核巨細胞，約五個大小一致、分開的圓形核，細胞質嗜酸性，即蝕骨細胞（osteoclast）；可與單一分葉核的巨核細胞區分。
features: Multinucleated giant cell with about five uniform, separate, round-to-oval nuclei
Cell sits in a shallow resorption bay (Howship lacuna) on the surface of a bony trabecula
Adjacent lamellar bone with an osteocyte in its lacuna
Marrow space with scattered hematopoietic cells and hyperchromatic lobulated cells (likely megakaryocytes)
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy section shows a bony trabecula with a multinucleated giant cell applied to its surface within a shallow resorption bay. The cell contains multiple separate, uniform round nuclei and moderate eosinophilic cytoplasm, features of an osteoclast. The adjacent marrow space contains scattered hematopoietic cells, including hyperchromatic lobulated forms likely representing megakaryocytes. Findings represent a normal osteoclast engaged in bone resorption; increased numbers would suggest high bone turnover such as hyperparathyroidism or metastatic disease.

ddx.vs: Megakaryocytes have a single large multilobated nucleus and sit within the marrow space adjacent to sinusoids rather than on bone surfaces with multiple discrete nuclei.
Osteoblasts are mononuclear cells with an eccentric nucleus, basophilic cytoplasm and paranuclear hof that line bone in rows during bone formation.
Granulomatous giant cells lie within epithelioid histiocyte aggregates away from bone surfaces and are not seated in resorption lacunae.
Tumor giant cells show nuclear pleomorphism, hyperchromasia and atypical mitoses, unlike the uniform bland nuclei of an osteoclast.
